result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane intersection with a long pedestrian crossing distance and minimal protective infrastructure. While a high-visibility crosswalk is present on one leg, the overall environment is dominated by vehicle traffic with few visible amenities for pedestrian safety or comfort.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for an extended period without a refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main intersection leg on the right.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, which can lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install visible pedestrian signals with countdown timers to improve crossing safety.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous sidewalk and a signalized intersection with a marked crosswalk. However, the roadway design lacks physical traffic calming or pedestrian refuge islands, potentially exposing pedestrians to higher-speed traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of physical buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the roadway with only a curb for separation, offering little protection from vehicles.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The intersection requires pedestrians to cross the entire roadway without a median refuge island.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Buffered Bike Lane
interventions.description: Implement a buffered or protected bike lane to provide additional separation between pedestrians and motor vehicles.

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility continental crosswalk and a sidewalk with a curb ramp, providing basic pedestrian access. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and traffic calming measures, leaving pedestrians reliant on vehicle signals for crossing.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle traffic lights which may not account for pedestrian clearance intervals.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners where signals would typically be mounted.

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Exposure
hazards.description: The wide roadway width increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the marked crosswalk in the foreground.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane or shoulder to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, multi-lane intersection with a marked crosswalk that lacks a connecting sidewalk in the foreground. The absence of pedestrian signals and refuge islands, combined with long crossing distances, creates a high-risk environment for non-motorized users.

hazards.description: The crosswalk begins in an area with no paved sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk on the road shoulder or grass.
